then.text: I've signed, duck. Go on, get it to the Wolds.

else.text: A petition against slavery? Course I'll sign. My husband went to sea at fourteen and worked like a slave half his life, and he'd tell you himself he was a free man. That's the difference that matters.
There. Mrs E. Fenwick, Hessle Road. Spelt right.
One name on the petition. Next: the churchwarden at Rudston, out on the Wolds.
Come in, duck, mind the step. Every house on this road had someone at sea.
When the trawlers came in, the whole road came out. When one didn't come in, the whole road knew by teatime.

then.text: Wear it with the pattern facing out. It's a Hull pattern. Proud of it.

else.text: A gansey for a new deckie? I've one on the needles now. Oiled wool, close knit, so the spray runs off.
Off you go. Mind you come back in it.
You pull on the gansey. It smells faintly of sheep and the sea.
Ganseys, they're called. Fishermen's jumpers. Every family had its own stitch, and every port its own pattern.
